purpose: Kafka-driven email classification engine that predicts spam, phishing, and newsletter verdicts.

domain_model.description: Emails flow through a Kafka-consumed pipeline of ordered classifiers that assign verdicts and risk levels.

bounded_contexts.name: Classification
bounded_contexts.description: Pipeline of classifiers that evaluate emails and produce verdicts.

ubiquitous_language.verdict: Enum outcome of classification: Clean, Spam, Newsletter, SuspiciousNewsletter, Skipped, Timedout, Unknown.
ubiquitous_language.risk-level: Numeric 0-9 severity score assigned alongside the verdict.
ubiquitous_language.classifier: Ordered prediction unit in the pipeline, each with a unique ClassifierID.
ubiquitous_language.pipeline: Ordered chain of classifiers that processes an email to produce a verdict.

bounded_contexts.name: Ingestion
bounded_contexts.description: Kafka consumer that deserializes, decompresses, and dispatches email requests.

ubiquitous_language.request-type: Integer 1-6 distinguishing prediction, notification, training, query, ping, test-connection.
ubiquitous_language.fml-sn: FortiMail serial number identifying the sending appliance.

bounded_contexts.name: Persistence
bounded_contexts.description: Aerospike, MongoDB, and MySQL stores for email records, config, and user profiles.

ubiquitous_language.europa-database: Facade class wrapping all database operations (Aerospike, MongoDB, legacy MySQL).
ubiquitous_language.home-domain: Customer-owned domain configured per API key.

stack.runtime: Python 3.12 on Fedora 39, deployed via Docker Compose with 4 application containers (fai, merge-usr-pro, dbclean, vector-srv) plus Kafka, Aerospike, MongoDB, Qdrant, OpenSearch, Prometheus, Grafana.

groups.name: Classification Engine
groups.description: Kafka consumer, pipeline orchestration, classifier chain, and ML/LLM intelligence.

groups.name: Data Layer
groups.description: Database facade, email domain model, and configuration management.

groups.name: Operations
groups.description: Background workers, vector management API, and deployment infrastructure.

actors.description: FortiMail appliance that publishes email classification requests to Kafka and consumes verdict responses.
Operator or tool that uses the vector-srv REST API to vectorize text or release vectors to Qdrant.
Docker Compose restart policy keeps merge-usr-pro and dbclean running continuously.

components.name: Kafka Consumer
components.description: Consumes FML-REQUEST topic, deserializes gzip+JSON messages, dispatches to pipeline via thread pool.

components.name: Classification Pipeline
components.description: Orchestrates ordered classifier chain, handles caching, trusted-sender bypass, and verdict adjustment.

components.name: Classifier Chain
components.description: 20+ classifiers with abstract Classifier interface, dynamically loaded from MongoDB config, sorted by ClassifierID priority.

components.name: Vector Service
components.description: Flask REST API exposing /vectorize and /release endpoints for text-to-vector conversion and Qdrant storage.

components.name: Feature Extractor
components.description: Sentence-transformer vectorizer and ML feature extraction using HuggingFace models and scikit-learn.

components.name: LLM Client
components.description: HTTP client calling an external LLM inference server with TTL cache and Prometheus instrumentation.

components.name: Europa Database
components.description: Facade over Aerospike, MongoDB, and legacy MySQL providing config, email storage, sender stats, and user profiles.

components.name: Background Workers
components.description: merge_usr_pro (hourly/daily profile aggregation) and dbclean (record aging) containers running as long-lived loops.

components.name: Email Model
components.description: EmailInfo domain object parsing raw Kafka messages into structured fields with scoring, normalization, and hashing.

flows.name: Email Classification
flows.description: End-to-end flow from Kafka message to verdict response.
flows.trigger: FortiMail publishes email to FML-REQUEST Kafka topic.

steps.transform: gzip decompress, JSON parse, extract response_topic

flows.name: Classifier Chain Execution
flows.description: Ordered evaluation through 20+ classifiers, short-circuiting on first non-Unknown verdict.

steps.condition: verdict == Unknown AND not timed out
FNSubmission rewrite rules and TEST_FP flag

flows.name: Vector Similarity Scoring
flows.description: Text vectorization and Qdrant-based similarity search for content classification.

steps.action: evaluate expression tree rules on matches
steps.transform: risk_level assignment based on rule evaluation

flows.name: User Profile Aggregation
flows.description: Periodic merging and cleanup of per-user email activity profiles in Aerospike.
flows.trigger: merge_usr_pro container loop triggers at minute==1 each hour.

steps.action: daily aggregate and cleanup at hour==1
steps.to_state: daily aggregates created, old detail records purged

state.stores: Email records, sender stats, URL stats, user profiles (detail/hourly/daily), cached emails.

concurrency.mechanism: Aerospike CAS via generation count, UDF-based aggregation
concurrency.conflicts: last-write-wins for simple records, UDF-based merge for profiles

state.stores: Pipeline config (cfg_pipelines), classifier registry (cfg_models), home domains, email addresses, malformed/phishing rules, URI patterns.
Email text vectors (768-dim) with category, rule, and language payloads.

concurrency.conflicts: duplicate check via similarity search threshold 0.9

state.stores: LLM classification results keyed by MD5 hash of query content.

concurrency.conflicts: no locking, potential race on concurrent writes (benign for cache)

events.name: FML-REQUEST
events.data: JSON-wrapped gzip-compressed email fields (email_id, request_type, fml_sn, api_key, headers, body, SPF/DKIM results).

events.name: FML-RESPONSE-{fml_sn}
events.data: JSON verdict response (email_id, verdict, risk_level, classifier_id).

failure_modes.trigger: Kafka broker becomes unreachable or FML-REQUEST topic is deleted.

cascade.effect: Consumer poll returns UNKNOWN_TOPIC_OR_PART, consumer closes.
No verdict responses produced, FortiMail gets no classification.

failure_modes.impact: All email classification stops. FortiMail appliances receive no verdict, emails pass through unscanned.
recovery: Restart fai container after Kafka is healthy

cascade.effect: Email cache lookups, sender stats, email inserts all fail.
merge_usr_pro and dbclean loops log errors and retry every 30s.

failure_modes.impact: Classification continues with degraded accuracy (no sender history, no caching). Emails still processed but without historical context. Profile aggregation halts.

cascade.effect: Config loading fails, classifier discovery fails.
Pipeline uses stale in-memory config until restart. New classifiers cannot be registered.

failure_modes.impact: Classification continues with stale config. Config changes from admin UI are not picked up. On restart, fai container fails to initialize.

failure_modes.trigger: LLM inference server responds slowly or is unreachable.

cascade.effect: requests.post times out after LLM_TIMEOUT seconds (default 4s).
LlmClassifier returns Verdict.Unknown, next classifier in chain evaluates.

failure_modes.impact: Emails that would have been caught by LLM analysis pass to downstream classifiers. Latency increases by timeout duration per email.
recovery: LLM cache provides some resilience for repeated content

failure_modes.impact: Vector similarity classification disabled. Other classifiers continue. Vector-srv API is unavailable.
detection: vector-srv /health endpoint returns 200 but operations fail

failure_modes.trigger: All THREAD_POOL_SIZE threads (default 8) are occupied by slow email classifications.

cascade.effect: executor.submit blocks, consumer.poll is not called, Kafka consumer falls behind.
Commit interval missed, risk of reprocessing on restart.

failure_modes.impact: Classification latency increases, backpressure builds up in Kafka. FortiMail may timeout waiting for verdicts.

evidence.note: Ordered chain of classifiers where each processes or passes the email.
Abstract Classifier base class with interchangeable predict() implementations.
Each classifier can handle (return verdict) or pass (return Unknown) to the next.
queue.Queue used for email insert threads and archive thread.
confluent_kafka Consumer with poll/commit cycle writing to Aerospike/MongoDB.
EuropaDatabase wraps Aerospike, MongoDB, and MySQL behind a single interface.
Dynamic classifier instantiation via __import__ and getattr from MongoDB config.
TTLCache for LLM results and Aerospike cache for email verdicts.
Prometheus Histogram and Counter metrics for latency and request counts.
INI-based config with typed defaults, loaded from file. Database-backed dynamic config via MongoDB.
SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers with threading.Event for graceful shutdown.
database.py is 3615 lines; emailinfo.py is 1942 lines. Both handle many unrelated concerns.
13+ bare except: clauses that silently catch and discard all exceptions.
Classifiers directly import EuropaDatabase and call its methods. No abstraction layer between classifiers and storage.
Numeric thresholds (scores, counts) scattered as literals across classifiers without named constants.
Config spread across INI file, Python defaults, MongoDB documents, and hardcoded values.

gaps.relevance: No retry logic on any external dependency except implicit Kafka consumer reconnection.
gaps.recommendation: Add retry with backoff to Aerospike, MongoDB, and Qdrant client calls.

gaps.recommendation: Add health/readiness endpoints to the fai container for Docker healthcheck and monitoring.

gaps.relevance: JSONLogFormatter exists but some code paths use print() statements.
gaps.recommendation: Replace all print() calls with logger calls to ensure consistent structured JSON output.

gaps.relevance: Kafka message parsing has basic field checks but no schema validation.

gaps.relevance: No trace ID propagation across Kafka messages, LLM calls, or database operations.

debt.interpretation: Significant structural debt driven by god objects, bare exception handling, hardcoded secrets, and zero resilience patterns across 6 external dependencies.

violations.detail: database.py is 3615 lines handling Aerospike, MongoDB, MySQL, config loading, email queries, sender stats, and user profiles.
emailinfo.py is 1942 lines combining parsing, normalization, scoring, hashing, and accessor logic.
Default MySQL password 'Spam123#db' in config.py:53 and hardcoded AES key in encryption.py:10.
No circuit breaker, retry, or timeout on Aerospike, MongoDB, or Qdrant calls.
All 3 vector-srv endpoints have no authentication. /release writes directly to production Qdrant store.
Classifiers directly import and call EuropaDatabase methods. No repository abstraction.
13+ bare except: clauses silently discard exceptions, masking failures.
Config spread across INI file, Python defaults, MongoDB documents, and inline literals.
Exception details leaked to API clients via str(e).
Main fai service has /metrics but no /health or /readyz endpoint for container orchestration.
Numeric thresholds scattered as literals (7, 13, 50, 2048) without named constants.
print() used for logging in 10+ locations instead of structured JSON logger.
3 TODO comments for ATO handling that has not been implemented.

recommendations.title: Rotate hardcoded secrets and move to environment variables
recommendations.description: The default MySQL password 'Spam123#db' and hardcoded AES key are committed to source. Move all secrets to environment variables or a secrets manager. Rotate the AES key and MySQL password immediately.

recommendations.title: Add authentication to vector-srv endpoints
recommendations.description: All vector-srv endpoints are unauthenticated. /release writes to the production Qdrant store. Add API key authentication at minimum, ideally a shared secret or mTLS.

recommendations.title: Add resilience wrappers to external dependency calls
recommendations.description: None of the 6 external dependencies have circuit breakers, retries, or timeouts. Add a resilience wrapper (e.g., tenacity for retry, pybreaker for circuit breaking) to Aerospike, MongoDB, and Qdrant client calls. This single change addresses both the missing-resilience and the cascading failure risks.

recommendations.title: Split database.py into domain-scoped repositories
recommendations.description: database.py (3615 lines) handles Aerospike email ops, MongoDB config, MySQL legacy, sender stats, and user profiles. Split into AerospikeEmailRepository, MongoConfigRepository, SenderStatsService, and UserProfileService. This also addresses the tight-coupling issue as classifiers would depend on interfaces rather than the god object.

recommendations.title: Replace bare except clauses with specific exception handling
recommendations.description: 13+ bare except: clauses silently discard exceptions. Replace with specific exception types and ensure errors are logged. This will surface hidden failures that currently go unnoticed.

recommendations.title: Consolidate configuration into a single source
recommendations.description: Config is spread across INI file defaults, Python hardcoded defaults, and MongoDB documents. Establish MongoDB as the single source of truth for runtime config, with the INI file providing only bootstrap values (Kafka, DB connection strings).

recommendations.title: Extract named constants for classifier thresholds
recommendations.description: Numeric thresholds are scattered as magic numbers. Move to named constants in a shared thresholds module or to MongoDB config for runtime tuning.
